submissions.title: OpenAI and SoftBank Commit $1 Billion to SB Energy, Launching 1.2 GW Stargate Site in Texas
submissions.excerpt: OpenAI and SoftBank Commit $1 Billion to SB Energy, Launching 1.2 GW Stargate Site in Texas
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker currently shows Stargate Milam County with power blank (site named by OpenAI, no capacity recorded). Jan 2026 reporting on SoftBank/SB Energy's $1B commitment discloses a 1.2 GW campus target -- recommend recording as an ANNOUNCED-target ESTIMATE only, explicitly basis: site power / full-build target. Epoch AI's independent site-by-site tracker separately estimates near-term capacity at only ~0.3 GW initially, so do NOT record 1.2GW as IT load or as anything close to current state.

claims.methodology: Announced full-campus target (SoftBank/SB Energy $1B commitment, Jan 2026), not an operator statement of current or near-term IT load. Basis: site power / full-build target, IT-vs-site unclear. Epoch AI's independent estimate puts near-term capacity at ~0.3 GW initially -- a large gap that argues for LOW confidence and against treating 1.2GW as anything but a target.

submissions.title: Chevron to fuel massive Microsoft data center in Texas using natural gas
submissions.excerpt: expected to consume nearly 2.7 gigawatts of electricity, equivalent to the power needed to run about 2 million homes
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker records Microsoft Pecos at 2000 MW (estimate, basis unstated), sourced to Microsoft's own 'approximately 2 gigawatts' blog language. Same-day reporting on Chevron's 'Project Kilby' 20-year gas-plant PPA describes a larger 2.67 GW figure, and CNBC's own phrasing describes this generation capacity as what the data center will 'consume' -- a site/generation-vs-IT-load conflation risk. Recommend a note distinguishing Microsoft's ~2GW datacenter figure from Chevron's 2.67GW gas-plant supply deal so the estimatedMw field isn't later overwritten with the larger generation number.

claims.methodology: Basis: generation / gas-plant supply capacity (Chevron Project Kilby, 20-year PPA), not IT load. Reported separately from Microsoft's own ~2GW datacenter capacity figure; multiple outlets conflate the two. Recorded as context only, to prevent future conflation -- not a proposed replacement for the existing 2000MW estimate.

submissions.title: Oracle and OpenAI's Abilene expansion saga detailed: 600MW expansion gets scrapped, as larger 4.5GW agreement remains on track
submissions.excerpt: Oracle and OpenAI's Abilene expansion saga detailed: 600MW expansion gets scrapped, as larger 4.5GW agreement remains on track
submissions.note: AUDIT: Stargate Abilene carries the tracker's oldest confirmed_power_mw figure (200 MW, sourced to an Oracle statement from April 2026) -- one of only 3 confirmed rows in the whole database, so it gets extra scrutiny every week. Since April, Oracle/OpenAI scrapped a planned 600MW expansion beyond the 1.2GW cap (March 2026) after financing issues and a multi-day winter cooling outage; a separate 4.5GW multi-site Oracle-OpenAI deal reportedly remains on track. None of this is reflected in analystNotes. Recommend: (a) timestamp the 200MW confirmed figure as 'as of April 2026' rather than presenting it as today's state -- Epoch's independent tracking now estimates ~421MW IT operating; (b) add the expansion-cancellation/cooling-outage context to analystNotes so readers understand the 1.2GW estimate carries real execution risk.

submissions.title: Lordstown continues navigating lawsuit from data center developer
submissions.excerpt: $3.6 billion, 1.65 million-square-foot data center on 133 acres on the former GM site
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker records Stargate Lordstown with power/capex/square-footage all blank ('site confirmed by OpenAI; no per-site capacity published'). A lawsuit filed by the site's developer (Bristolville 25 LLC, suing the village for a writ of mandamus to process permits) discloses concrete project figures: $3.6B capex, 133 acres, 1.65M sq ft. Also worth noting: Lordstown Village Council imposed a Jan-Jul 4 2026 moratorium on AI data center permitting, with an explicit carve-out for the unrelated SoftBank/Foxconn AI-manufacturing tenancy at the same former-GM site -- the tracker's single Lordstown row may be conflating the Bristolville-developed data center with the separate SoftBank/Foxconn manufacturing operation. Recommend recording the $3.6B capex figure and clarifying in analystNotes which entity/use is which.

claims.methodology: Figure disclosed via the developer's own court filing (writ of mandamus lawsuit against Lordstown Village), reported by Spectrum News 1 and corroborated by WKBN. Describes the data center project the developer is trying to get permitted, not construction already underway.

submissions.title: Project Jupiter lawsuit to proceed in Doña Ana County, judge orders review of data center incentives
submissions.excerpt: judge orders review of the commission's approval of $165 billion in industrial revenue bonds
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker's Stargate Dona Ana County row (power/capex deliberately blank -- correct, since no capacity has been disclosed) is missing a material development: an ongoing lawsuit (New Mexico Environmental Law Center v. Dona Ana County) over $165B in industrial revenue bonds/incentives for the project ('Project Jupiter'), plus a separate finding that the developers missed January and April 2026 job-hire reporting deadlines required under the incentive agreement. This doesn't change any numeric field (still correctly blank) but is exactly the kind of execution/compliance risk that belongs in analystNotes for a project still carrying UNDER_CONSTRUCTION status. Caution: do not record any 'first gigawatt of Nvidia systems' language seen in some coverage as MW power -- it describes planned chip deployment, not disclosed site capacity.

submissions.title: Neom to start building Oxagon AI data centre 'in months'
submissions.excerpt: We expect to break ground in the next two to three months and get on with these AI factories.
submissions.note: AUDIT: analystNotes currently state 'no construction on this campus is documented as of mid-2026.' DataVolt CEO Rajit Nanda told AGBI (Aug 2026; exact publication day not independently confirmed, recommend verifying) that groundbreaking is expected within two to three months. This is a developer statement of intent, not confirmed construction, but it supersedes the 'no construction documented' framing and should be reflected. No change recommended to the existing 1500MW/$5B announced-target figures.

submissions.title: Kevin O'Leary pins water licence for $70-billion data centre project on a small Alberta municipality
submissions.excerpt: First Nation in court to challenge proposed Wonder Valley AI data centre project in northern Alberta
submissions.note: AUDIT: analystNotes cite The Logic's Dec 2025 skeptical framing but miss two subsequent 2026 developments: (1) April 2026 -- Alberta exempted the project from a full provincial Environmental Impact Assessment 'due to its proposed use of standard power and water systems,' while confirming other permits (air/land/water technical assessments, AUC) are still required; (2) Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation is pursuing a judicial review (arguments heard June 2026) of a Water Act licence granted for the project, after the Environmental Appeals Board dismissed an earlier appeal (April 17 2026 decision). Neither confirms nor further discredits the project's near-term credibility -- recommend adding both as analystNotes context given the project's already-skeptical framing.

submissions.title: Lambda Plans to Open KCMO AI Factory in Early 2026
submissions.excerpt: expected to launch in early 2026 with 24MW of capacity, and the potential to scale up to more than 100MW
submissions.note: AUDIT: tracker records expectedOpeningDate as 2026-06-30, but both the cited PRNewswire release and independent Ingram's coverage describe the launch target as 'early 2026,' which conventionally means Q1 (Jan-Mar), not end of Q2. Recommend tightening expectedOpeningDate toward Q1 2026 (e.g. 2026-03-31) unless a more specific date is found, and separately noting that as of today (2026-08-10) no source confirms the facility has actually launched/energized -- it may already be running behind even its own stated target.
